mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return distribution in declining FEDFUNDS periods shows no statistically significant positive mean (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% for 3 consecutive months, it indicates restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative in FEDFUNDS > 4.5% periods (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and decline in UNRATE signals tightening policy during strong labor market conditions, increasing cost of capital and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
regime_hint: tightening cycle with strong labor market
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls (t-test p > 0.05) or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion with UNRATE < 3.5%, a further decline signals overheating and potential central bank intervention, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly negative in UNRATE < 3.5% periods (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand for housing, driving economic expansion and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns show no statistically significant positive mean in rising HOUST periods (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts exceed 1,400,000 units for 3 consecutive months, it signals an overheated housing market that may trigger correction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative in HOUST > 1400 periods (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and GDP (GDPC1) over 3 months signals economic contraction, increasing recession risk and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly negative in declining INDPRO and GDPC1 periods (t-test p > 0.05) or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate falls below 3.5% for 3 consecutive months, it indicates a tight labor market that may trigger aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in UNRATE < 3.5% periods (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
